proves.claim: clause 1: a real release reports committed open custody and a distinct actionable nonzero cleanup failure when real non-forced Git removal refuses a locked fixture worktree, without deleting its folder, registration or branch; clause 2: refusal and ordinary recovery preserve their behavior.

cli.release-committed-cleanup.retains-lo.why: An exception after durable release conceals that ownership already ended and invites a duplicate release or unsafe cleanup.

proves.claim: clause 1: a real release from its own item tree reports committed state, one release event and actual deferred Git refusal with retained custody in text and JSON; clause 2: pre-release refusal and ordinary clean deferred recovery preserve behavior.

cli.release-committed-cleanup.deferred-o.why: The release handler returns before deferred cleanup, so a late removal failure must not disappear behind an already flushed success.
